rationale: The facts are right: the report defines a used response as one whose text was copied, and Agent ratings counts positive or negative ratings. The defect is a leak. findings:
Checks 11 and 22 leak: the goal's judged matches only Agent ratings. Fix: replace prompt with: Lindqvist Freight runs Dynamics 365 Contact Center standalone, and Copilot analytics is enabled. Last month's Copilot analytics report shows 25 percent for Percentage of Copilot AI responses used. A manager concludes that representatives found the other 75 percent of the responses wrong.

You need to tell the manager what the 25 percent measures.

What does the 25 percent measure? Replace options with a: The share of Copilot responses from which representatives copied text; b: The share of Copilot responses that representatives rated positively; c: The share of Copilot responses that representatives sent to customers; d: The share of engaged conversations in which representatives used Copilot. Delete option e. Keep correctOptionIds [a]. Replace answer with: The share of Copilot responses from which representatives copied text. Replace explanation with: In the Copilot analytics report, Number of responses used is the number of times text from a Copilot response was copied, and Percentage of Copilot AI responses used is the percentage of responses that were copied. So the 25 percent is a copy rate, and a response that wasn't copied wasn't necessarily judged wrong. Representatives' judgments are counted separately by Agent ratings in the Satisfaction section, the number of times representatives rated a Copilot response positively or negatively. Replace optionExplanations with a: Correct. The report defines Percentage of Copilot AI responses used as the percentage of responses that were copied. b: Fails. Ratings are a separate metric, Agent ratings, which counts how many times representatives rated a Copilot response positively or negatively. c: Fails. The report counts a response as used when text from it was copied, not when it was sent to a customer. d: Fails. That is Percentage of conversations using Copilot AI, the percentage of engaged conversations that used Copilot. It counts conversations, not responses. The evidence entry stays as it is.

rationale: The answer pair is right under the stated settings, and every distractor fails for a documented reason. The defects are leaks and an unstated preview dependency. findings:
Checks 22, 26, 27 and 32 leak, and an unstated preview setting. Fix: change kind to single. Replace prompt with: Greenhaven Insurance handles claims over SMS through a push messaging workstream in Dynamics 365 Contact Center. Representative affinity is turned on for the workstream, and its notification template has Autoassign work items set to Yes. Microsoft labels Autoassign work items a preview setting, and Greenhaven has accepted the preview terms. Conversation orchestration is set up, and each CSR's conversation limit has been set in Enhanced user management.

Today, when a customer replies to a waiting SMS conversation, it goes back to the CSR who handled it. Managers want it to go back to that CSR only if the CSR is in a presence the managers choose and has fewer conversations open across all channels than their limit, which can be higher than their capacity. Otherwise, the next best CSR in the queue should get it.

You need to configure this behavior.

What should you do? Replace options with a: Publish a Keep the same expert for async chats playbook with the presences, active conversation limit and next best fallback; b: Publish an Assign to a previous or preferred expert playbook that checks presence and a 30-day recency window, with next best fallback; c: Set each CSR's work item limit in the SMS capacity profile equal to their conversation limit, and turn on Assignment blocking; d: Map each customer's contact to their last CSR in Preferred representative routing, with the next best representative fallback. Delete option e. Set correctOptionIds to [a]. Replace answer with: Publish a Keep the same expert for async chats playbook with the presences, the active conversation limit and the next best expert fallback. Replace explanation with: Representative affinity already reconnects a returning asynchronous conversation with the CSR who handled it, regardless of that CSR's capacity and presence, as long as the notification template's Autoassign work items is Yes. The Keep the same expert for async chats playbook adds the checks managers want, and its prerequisite is that representative affinity is enabled for the workstream. It checks the configured presences and compares the CSR's capacity-occupying conversations across all channels with their active conversation limit, reconnecting even when the limit exceeds the capacity profile. If the CSR fails a check, it assigns the next best expert or keeps the chat unassigned, as configured. New conversations are still governed by capacity profiles. Replace optionExplanations with a: Correct. This playbook applies to queues where representative affinity is enabled. For a returning asynchronous chat, it checks the configured presences and the CSR's active conversation limit across all channels, even when the limit exceeds the capacity profile, and otherwise assigns the next best expert in the queue. b: Fails. This playbook runs when a conversation is routed to a queue and checks presence, queue membership and a recency window of up to 30 days. It doesn't check the active conversation limit. c: Fails. Representative affinity reassigns a returning conversation regardless of the CSR's capacity and presence, and managers want a limit that can be higher than capacity. Assignment blocking only stops automatic assignment of new work items once the work item limit is met. d: Fails. Preferred representative routing assigns a contact to representatives you map in the matrix and skips the capacity check. It doesn't follow the CSR who last handled the conversation or check a conversation limit.
